messages:
alex: heads-up — after enabling the larger micro-batch window (coalesce_delay=4ms, jitter=1.5ms) we're seeing p99 regressions for short sequences (<32 tokens). observed spike ~18% at tail. attaching profiler notes below.

maria: saw similar in canary earlier, looks like kernel selector flips to the fallback path more often with these batch shapes.

jun: quick pprof dump I pulled this morning:
```
CPU: aggregate
 - memcpy: 30.4%
 - kernel_dispatch (int8_fallback): 24.7%
 - kv_lookup_lock: 18.1%
 - batching_coalesce_wait: 12.2%
```

rajesh: fwiw kv miss rate jumped from ~2% -> ~9% when coalesce_delay increased. miss latency also amplified because misses occur during heavier kernel contention.

alex: hypothesis: longer coalesce windows increase effective contention and push many short requests to a codepath that triggers a kernel fallback plus KV staleness penalties. two levers to try: reduce coalesce_delay (and jitter) to reduce latency for short seq, or keep delay but add async kv-prefetch / softer kernel selector threshold.

maria: suggested experiment matrix:
 - A (latency-first): coalesce_delay=2ms, jitter=0.5ms, selector_threshold=8 (baseline)
 - B (throughput-first w/ mitigations): coalesce_delay=4ms, jitter=1.5ms, enable async_kv_prefetch=true, selector_threshold=6
Add metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, kv_miss_rate, kv_miss_latency_p99, kernel_switch_rate, cost_per_1k_tokens.

yang: I can run 5% production canary for each with route param `?canary=cb-window` — will label traces.

infra-bot: deploy triggered by yang for route /v1/generate?canary=cb-window — build #4521.

jun: one more note: kernel selector currently switches on batch_size >= 8; lowering to 6 reduces fallback frequency for our short-heavy workload. but be careful: could increase mem pressure on fast-path kernel. add mem_used and kernel_latency_by_batch_size to dashboard.

rajesh: also consider moving KV prefetch earlier in request lifecycle (estimate keys from prompt prefix). cheap heuristic: if prefix length < 16 and model warmed, prefetch next-kv for top-3 tokens. cheap wins.

alex: agreed. plan: run A and B concurrently (independent canaries) for 2 hours each, collect metrics, then a short profiling run with `--trace-alloc` on the worst cohort. back-of-envelope pass/fail: p99 no worse than +5% and kv_miss_latency_p99 < 2x baseline.

maria: I created a dashboard: https://internal.redwood/dash/eng-runtime/cb-window-expt and added panels for all metrics.

yang: starting canary A now (5% traffic). will post results in ~2h.

alex: thanks — if you see kernel_switch_rate > 10% or kv_miss_rate > 6% abort early. otherwise let run the full window. :thumbsup:

maria: tagging @jun for the tracing step once we have the worst cohort.

jun: on it — I'll prep a lightweight flamegraph job and a pprof capture script.

alex: appreciated. sync at 1pm PST to make a call after both runs.

yang: noted, starting.

alex: one tiny config snippet if helpful (will push to infra repo in a bit):
```yaml
coalesce: 
  delay_ms: 2000  # 2ms -> experiment A
  jitter_ms: 500  # 0.5ms
kernel_selector: 
  batch_threshold: 6  # lowered in experiment B
kv: 
  async_prefetch: true  # B only
```

maria: nice, I'll add those as feature flags so we can flip without full deploy.

alex: cool — keep notes in this thread and drop raw traces to /tmp/cb-window-traces with names tagged by canary id.

yang: copy that.

alex: thanks everyone.
